title: 1. The Trail That Did Not Walk
description: Chapter 1 of 3 of “The Case of the Missing Star”. Read in order.

cover.alt: The Case of the Missing Star

illustration.alt: They decorate for a party; the star disappears, leaving an empty hook and two trails in the mud.

lines: Luna and her little brother Nico are helping Pico the stork prepare a party at the station.
A large yellow star will be their special decoration.
blocks.title: Getting ready

lines: Blue ribbon with white dots holds the star in place.
Its bow looks loose and flutters in the breeze as Pico moves a cart underneath.
blocks.title: The hanging star

lines: When the children turn back, the hook is empty.
They did not see the star disappear, so they cannot yet explain how it left its place.
blocks.title: It's gone!

lines: The wet ground holds two different trails: little pawprints towards the garden and two long lines towards the workshop.
Which should they investigate first?
blocks.title: Two trails

variants.retryFeedback: Look at the hook first, then at the trails on the ground.

variants.prompt: What must they learn before saying someone took it?
variants.retryFeedback: Look at the hook first, then at the trails on the ground.

illustration.alt: They follow pawprints to a cat, search by the bench, and return to the other trail.

lines: Nico follows the pawprints, wondering whether they lead to someone who passed near the decoration.
Luna joins him, remembering that a guess still needs evidence.
blocks.title: Trail to the garden

lines: The marks end beside a black-and-white cat resting near the bench.
Its little paws offer an explanation for the small prints along the garden path.
blocks.title: The cat by the bench

lines: They search around and under the bench but find no star.
This tells them where they did not find it, not who might have moved it.
blocks.title: Not here

lines: Back at the fork, the children decide to examine the other trail.
Rather than defend their first guess, they will look for something they have missed.
blocks.title: Back to the crossing

variants.prompt: Where do the little pawprints lead?

options.text: To the cat beside the bench

variants.correctFeedback: That’s it! To the cat beside the bench.
variants.retryFeedback: Pawprints show who passed; check whether they also found the decoration.

variants.prompt: What can they say after searching beside the bench?

options.text: They did not find it there

variants.correctFeedback: That’s it! They did not find it there.
variants.retryFeedback: Pawprints show who passed; check whether they also found the decoration.

illustration.alt: Dotted ribbon beside wheel marks leads them to a window with a huge shadow.

lines: Luna spots a scrap of fabric caught on a twig beside the long muddy lines.
She crouches for a closer look without stepping on the trail.
blocks.title: The ribbon scrap

lines: The scrap is blue with white dots, matching the star's ribbon.
That links the two places, although it does not explain how the fabric travelled here.
blocks.title: The same dots

lines: The lines continue to a wooden door.
Luna keeps the ribbon scrap while Nico looks carefully at where the muddy trail enters the small workshop.
blocks.title: To the workshop

lines: A huge pointed silhouette fills the bright window.
Nico feels nervous, but Luna suggests finding its source before deciding what could be waiting inside.
blocks.title: A huge shadow

variants.prompt: What pattern is on the blue ribbon scrap?
variants.retryFeedback: Compare the ribbon pattern with the one at the beginning.

variants.prompt: What links the workshop trail to the star?

options.text: Matching ribbon beside the long lines

variants.correctFeedback: That’s it! Matching ribbon beside the long lines.
variants.retryFeedback: Compare the ribbon pattern with the one at the beginning.

stork.definition: A bird with a long beak and long legs.
stork.example: We saw a stork standing on one leg on the rooftop.

ribbon.definition: A narrow strip of fabric used for tying or decorating.
ribbon.example: She tied a red ribbon around the gift before giving it away.

bow.definition: A knot with loops that can be loosened by pulling an end.
bow.example: He tied a bow on his shoelaces so they wouldn't come undone.

hook.definition: A curved piece used to hang something.
hook.example: We hung the keys on a hook by the door.

pawprints.definition: Marks left by an animal’s feet.
pawprints.example: We followed the pawprints in the snow all the way to the doghouse.

trail.definition: Marks that show where something has passed.
trail.example: The dog followed the trail of the hidden toy across the yard.

workshop.definition: A place where things are made or repaired.
workshop.example: We took the bike to the workshop because the chain had come off.

silhouette.definition: The outline of a shape without its inner details.
silhouette.example: We recognized her silhouette against the light from the door.

evidence.definition: Information used to check an explanation.
evidence.example: She kept the photo as evidence that she arrived first.

muddy.example: His boots were muddy after walking through the field.

scrap.definition: A small piece left or torn from something.
scrap.example: He used a scrap of fabric to patch the torn backpack.

explanation.definition: An account of how or why something happened.
explanation.example: She gave a simple explanation for why she was late.

decoration.definition: Something used to make a place look special.
decoration.example: We hung paper decorations around the classroom for the party.

investigate.definition: To look carefully for facts that explain something.
investigate.example: The detective decided to investigate the strange noise in the attic.
